title: fix: broken upgrade compatibility test by defining GO_VERSION at workflow level
body:
The `upgrade-test.yaml` workflow has been failing because `actions/setup-go` receives an empty `go-version` input, producing `Warning: go-version input was not specified` followed by `/bin/sh: 1: version: not found`.

The composite action `.github/actions/e2e-base-setup/action.yaml` declares a top-level `env: GO_VERSION: "1.26.2"`, but **GitHub composite actions silently ignore top-level `env`**. Its `setup-go` step references `${{ env.GO_VERSION }}`, which only resolves when the *calling* workflow defines `GO_VERSION` in its own `env:` block. The sibling workflows (`e2e-workflow.yaml`, `ragengine-e2e-workflow.yaml`) do; `upgrade-test.yaml` did not.

### Changes

- **`.github/workflows/upgrade-test.yaml`**: add `GO_VERSION: "1.26.2"` to the workflow-level `env:`, matching the pattern in the other e2e workflows.
- **`.github/actions/e2e-base-setup/action.yaml`**: remove the misleading no-op top-level `env:` block so future maintainers don't assume it works.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/upgrade-test.yaml
env:
  OLD_CHART_VERSION: ${{ github.event.inputs.old_chart_version || '0.7.1' }}
  GO_VERSION: "1.26.2"   # added — consumed by ./.github/actions/e2e-base-setup
```

A more thorough follow-up would be to make the composite action self-contained (e.g., accept `go_version` as an `input` with a default), eliminating the implicit env-var contract with callers.
